app.title: SPHEREx Sky Tracker
app.tagline: See how the sky changes over time

welcome.lead: Find an object in NASA's SPHEREx infrared sky maps, compare its images from different dates and see how the sky changes.
welcome.privacyLogin: If you sign in, your search and list activity can be seen by the site administrator.
welcome.privacyGuest: As a guest, your activity is not linked to personal data such as an e-mail address.

hero.heading: SPHEREx re-maps the whole sky every six months
hero.body: SPHEREx surveys the entire sky in 102 colours (spectral channels) between 0.75 and 5 µm. Comparing images of the same region taken at different dates reveals comets, asteroids and fast-moving nearby stars as they change position.
hero.step1: Type an object name or coordinates
hero.step3: See the change with blink and difference images
hero.honest: A SPHEREx image is not a single-colour photograph: the wavelength changes from one edge of the image to the other. The site shows this clearly on every screen.

atlas.title: 3I/ATLAS — interstellar comet
atlas.body: SPHEREx observed this comet in August and December 2025; DR1 also has frames from March–April 2026. Frames are centred on the comet and played one by one.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.summary: This site records anonymous usage events to understand how it is used (e.g. which page was opened, which object was searched).
privacy.details: Recorded: a random session id, event type and time, searched object, browser family (e.g. "chrome") and a salted hash of your IP address that changes every day. The IP address itself is never stored. Records are deleted after 90 days. If you create an account, your e-mail is used only to send login codes. Data is not shared with third parties.
privacy.essentialNote: With "Essential only" no usage events are sent; the site still works fully.

result.title: Comparison result
result.honest: These values are computed directly from the data. Calibration, wavelength differences and atmospheric lines can mimic change; read the warnings below.

warnings.CHANNEL_WARN: Wavelengths are close but not equal (Δλ = {{dl}} nm, {{ratio}} × bandwidth). For sources with a sloped spectrum this alone changes the brightness.
warnings.CROSS_RELEASE: A and B come from different releases ({{a}} / {{b}}). {{fix}}
warnings.CROSS_RELEASE_FIXED: IRSA's QR3 flux correction (l3_flux_corrections) was applied to the QR2 image.
warnings.CROSS_RELEASE_NOFIX: The flux correction could not be applied; do not compare absolute brightness.
warnings.PIPELINE_DIFFERS: Different pipeline versions within the release ({{a}} / {{b}}): calibration and masking may differ.
warnings.NO_BACKGROUND: The whole field is flagged as source (e.g. a large galaxy); no local background was subtracted.
warnings.NORMALIZATION_UNRELIABLE: Not enough field pixels for relative normalisation; none applied.
warnings.LOW_SNR: Low signal-to-noise on the target ({{snr}}); differences may be noise.
warnings.HIGH_MASK_FRACTION: {{pct}}% of epoch {{epoch}} pixels are masked (cosmic rays, ghosts, saturation…).
warnings.ATMOSPHERIC_LINE: Epoch {{epoch}} wavelength is near a time-variable, unsubtracted atmospheric line: {{lines}}.
warnings.TARGET_NEAR_EDGE: Epoch {{epoch}}: the target is close to the cutout edge.
warnings.PROPER_MOTION_APPLIED: The target position for each date uses SIMBAD proper motion (annual parallax ignored).
warnings.SATURATED_OR_MASKED_CORE: Epoch {{epoch}}: the target core is saturated or masked; no aperture photometry.
warnings.NO_PHOTOMETRY: Epoch {{epoch}}: not enough valid pixels in the aperture; brightness not measured.
warnings.DIFFERENT_TYPES: The two objects are of different types ({{a}} / {{b}}); the comparison is for illustration only.
